or_1_northeast_face.blurb: This is a stretch of tall cliff and buttress in the Smith Rock Group of Central Oregon's Smith Rock State Park. It holds about two dozen routes, mainly bolted single-pitch lines alongside a smaller set of trad climbs and one aid line. Grades run from the high 5.7s to the 5.12s, with most routes landing in the 5.10 to 5.11 range. The longer ridge and chimney lines go up to several pitches, so the face suits both a quick sport session and a bigger day out. Reaching the base means a walk along the river trail and up toward the pass, with the ridge routes involving some scrambling.

or_f_cocaine_gully.blurb: A steep, narrow gully at Smith Rock State Park, squeezed in with the Morning Glory Wall on one side and the West Ship on the other, and running beside its neighbour Aggro Gully. Nearly everything here is a bolted sport line on vertical to overhanging tuff, with a single crack as the lone trad route. The grade spread starts around 5.10 and climbs to 5.13, but the bulk of the routes sit in the 5.11 to 5.12 range, so this is a pump-heavy place for strong intermediates and up rather than a beginner venue. The gully walls throw shade in summer and can feel warm when the weather is cold.

or_mud_pile.blurb: The Mud Pile is a long north-south formation among the Marsupials, the cluster of pinnacles on the far side of the gorge at Smith Rock State Park, downhill from Brogan Spire. Most of its two dozen routes are bolted sport lines, with a handful of trad and aid options, including a long traverse. Grades start in the 5.7 range and stretch beyond 5.12, though the large majority are between 5.8 and 5.11, which makes it a good place for moderate leaders looking for newer routes away from the main walls. Expect a hike of some length to get to its base.

or_7_gods_and_monsters_wall.blurb: The far end of the Klinger Spring cliff line on the east side of Mt. Hood, this wall is named for the odd monster-like knobs along its top edge. It is the tallest part of the crag, with about two dozen routes that lean toward trad but include a good handful of bolted lines and one top-rope. Grades run from the 5.6 range up to 5.11, with most climbs between 5.8 and 5.10. Many two-pitch lines can be strung together into one sustained, pumpy pitch, and some require a 70 metre rope to lower safely, so bring a long cord and tie a stopper knot.

or_4_the_cathedral.blurb: The Cathedral is the busiest sector of the Rattlesnake crag in southwest Oregon's Rogue Valley, built around an arch-shaped formation with a window cut through its outer wall. Its two dozen routes are almost all bolted sport lines on welded tuff, plus a couple of trad lines and a top-rope variation. Climbing happens on the main wall inside the arch and on both sides of the window wall. Grades begin near 5.9 and reach 5.13, with the heart of the range at 5.10 to 5.12, so it rewards climbers working through the 5.11 and 5.12 grades. Light rain is usually workable here.
